questions.stem: How is a computer described in its basic form?

options.B: An electronic device that receives, processes, and produces data
options.C: A purely manual data entry tool
options.D: A device that only stores information

questions.explanation: The document defines a computer as an electronic device that can receive data, process it, and produce the result as an outcome.

questions.stem: In the computer data flow process, what is the result of processing known as?
questions.explanation: The text states that the result of the processing is known as output or information.

questions.stem: Which major part of the computer is described as the 'spirit or soul'?
questions.explanation: The document uses the analogy that hardware is the body while software is the spirit or soul.

questions.stem: What is the basis of machine language used by computers?
questions.explanation: Computers process numerical data in binary digital format, which is the basis of machine language.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a subsystem of a full-fledged computer system?
questions.explanation: A computer system comprises users, application software, systems software, operating system, and hardware.

questions.stem: The users' subsystem includes which of the following groups?

options.C: Only people who buy the computer

questions.explanation: The text explicitly defines the users' subsystem as comprising expert users, programmers/developers, and end-users.

questions.stem: Which characteristic refers to a computer's ability to perform different types of tasks?
questions.explanation: Versatility is listed as a characteristic of a computer, referring to its multi-tasking capabilities.

questions.stem: What defines computer hardware according to the document?

options.B: Any physical parts or components that contribute to a computer system
options.D: The code that runs the computer

questions.explanation: The document defines hardware as any physical parts or components contributing to the system.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of computer software?
questions.explanation: Google Chrome is listed as a computer software component in the comparison table.

questions.stem: How are Personal Computers (PCs) characterized in terms of user capacity?
questions.explanation: The text defines personal computers as single-user computers based on microprocessors.

questions.stem: Which computer type is specifically described as being 'relatively more powerful than PCs' but still 'single-user-based'?
questions.explanation: Workstations are described as more powerful than PCs while remaining single-user-based.

questions.stem: Which organizations are likely to own minicomputers according to the document?

options.C: Large organizations like NASA or CBN

questions.explanation: Minicomputers belong to large organizations such as NASRDA, NIMC, CBN, and NASA.

questions.stem: Mainframe computers can support approximately how many users simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Mainframes are multi-user systems that support thousands of users simultaneously.

questions.stem: What was the world's fastest supercomputer known on Top500 until early 2021?
questions.explanation: Until early 2021, the Chinese exascale system Fugaku was known as the world's fastest supercomputer.

questions.stem: Who is credited with inventing the first runner of digital programmable computers in 1833?
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage invented the first runner of digital programmable and general-purpose computers in 1833.

questions.stem: Which technology was the hallmark of First Generation computers (1940-1956)?
questions.explanation: The first generation showcased the use of vacuum tubes for logic circuitry.

questions.stem: What was a major drawback of first-generation computer systems?

options.D: They were too fast for users

questions.explanation: Drawbacks of first-generation systems included slower speed, excessive heat, and high cost.

questions.stem: Second-generation computers (1957-1963) replaced vacuum tubes with which component?
questions.explanation: In the second generation, transistors were used as the significant switching devices.

questions.stem: What technology defined the third generation of computers (1964-1971)?
questions.explanation: Integrated circuits were developed and used as switching devices during the third generation.

questions.stem: Fourth-generation computers are based on the invention of which component?
questions.explanation: Fourth-generation computers were based on the development of microprocessors as the CPU.

questions.stem: Which company was the first to design and develop microprocessors?
questions.explanation: The document states that Intel was the first company to design and develop microprocessors.

questions.stem: The fifth generation of computers (1990 to date) incorporates which concept?
questions.explanation: Fifth-generation computers incorporate multi-core technologies and artificial intelligence concepts.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a robot from the fifth generation?
questions.explanation: Sophia is explicitly listed as an example of a robot in the fifth-generation section.

questions.stem: What is described as the interface between system hardware, application software, and users?
questions.explanation: The operating system is software that interfaces between hardware, application software, and users.

questions.stem: Which type of software is designed to perform specific tasks like word processing or accounting?
questions.explanation: The document lists word processing and accounting as tasks carried out by software (later categorized under application software).

questions.stem: What happens to data in RAM when the computer power is turned off?

options.B: It is moved to the cloud

questions.explanation: RAM is non-persistent; if power is turned off, data and programs are erased automatically.

questions.stem: How much is 1 nanosecond in relation to a second?
questions.explanation: The document defines 1 nanosecond as 1 billionth of a second.

questions.stem: Which type of compact disc cannot be deleted or overwritten after being recorded once?
questions.explanation: For CD-R (Recordable), contents can be stored once and read several times but cannot be deleted or overwritten.

questions.stem: What is the storage capacity of a double-sided double-layer DVD?
questions.explanation: The document states a double-sided double-layer DVD has a capacity of 17 GB.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a pointing input device?
questions.explanation: The text identifies the mouse, trackball, and touchpad as examples of pointing input devices.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of an output device?

options.A: To enter data into the computer
options.B: To convert human-readable data to machine code
options.C: To display or physically reproduce results of processed data

questions.explanation: An output device displays, projects, or physically reproduces the results of data processed by a computer.

questions.stem: Which printer type uses a photoelectric drum and powdered ink?
questions.explanation: Laser printers use a photoelectric drum, powdered ink, and laser light to produce dots for printing.

questions.stem: What device is typically used for architectural blueprints and large high-quality engineering drawings?
questions.explanation: A plotter is used to generate hardcopy large drawings and architectural blueprints.

questions.stem: What is the main function of the motherboard's CMOS battery?

options.B: To provide backup for the system clock and BIOS setup

questions.explanation: The CMOS battery provides memory power backup for the system clock and system setup parameters in the BIOS chip.

questions.stem: Which component on the motherboard replaced a larger number of individual chips to control data flow?
questions.explanation: A chipset is a smaller set of chips that replaced a larger amount of chips to control data flow between components.

questions.stem: What is the unit for modern computer clock speeds mentioned in the text?
questions.explanation: The text mentions that nowadays, PCs have clock speeds greater than 3.2 billion pulses per second (3.2 GHz).

questions.stem: Which port transmits 8 bits of data simultaneously?
questions.explanation: While serial ports transmit one bit at a time, parallel ports transmit 8 bits of data simultaneously.

questions.stem: What is another name for microchips?
questions.explanation: Microchips are also known as chips or integrated circuits (IC).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a 'Don't' in computer maintenance best practices?

options.C: Ignore warning signs of hardware failure

questions.explanation: Ignoring warning signs of hardware failure is listed under the 'Don'ts' for maintenance.

questions.stem: How often should coolant be replaced in liquid-cooled computers?
questions.explanation: The document advises replacing coolant every 6-12 months for liquid-cooled systems.

questions.stem: What are computers on a network commonly called?
questions.explanation: Computers on a network are called nodes or hosts.

questions.stem: Which networking device is used to send information over a network cable?
questions.explanation: While a modem sends information over a communication line, a network card sends it over a network cable.

questions.stem: What term describes the physical arrangement and layout of computing resources in a network?
questions.explanation: Network Topology is the physical arrangement and layout of the computing shared resources.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a common example of network topology?
questions.explanation: Common examples listed are Bus, Star, Mesh, Ring, and Daisy chain.

questions.stem: Network performance is a function of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Performance is a function of the throughput, which involves transit and response times.

questions.stem: What is multi-core technology?

options.B: Two or more logical CPUs on the same processor chip

questions.explanation: Multi-core technology describes the operation of two or more logical CPUs on the same processor chip.

questions.stem: A 'dual-quad core' processor refers to how many total core processors?
questions.explanation: Dual quad cores refer to two sockets having four CPUs each, making a total of eight core processors.

questions.stem: What is an embedded system?

options.A: A computer that can be taken apart easily
options.B: A computer system with a dedicated function within a larger mechanical or electrical system
options.C: A system that only uses software

questions.explanation: Embedded systems have dedicated functions within larger mechanical or electrical systems.

questions.stem: What is an example of an embedded system mentioned in the text?
questions.explanation: An elevator controller is explicitly mentioned as an example of an embedded system.

questions.stem: What is specialized software used to operate in-built computers called?
questions.explanation: Embedded software is a specialized kind of portable software used to operate in-built computers.

questions.stem: Where are 'on-board computers' specifically configured and installed?

options.B: In mobile objects or vehicles like submarines and aircraft

questions.explanation: On-board computers are configured and installed in mobile objects or vehicles such as submarines, ships, and aircraft.

questions.stem: In a digital system, a binary digit (bit) has a value of either:
questions.explanation: A binary digit (bit) has a value of either 0 or 1.

questions.stem: How many bits make up 1 byte?
questions.explanation: The document states that 1 byte comprises 8 bits.

questions.stem: Which organization is mentioned as ensuring reliable computer networks for CBT exams?
questions.explanation: The text notes that JAMB ensures CBT centres have reliable computer networks.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common maintenance tool for Windows?
questions.explanation: Disk Cleanup is listed as a utility tool for Windows maintenance.

questions.stem: Which company is a manufacturer of computer motherboards?
questions.explanation: ASUS is listed as one of the popular motherboard manufacturers.

questions.stem: Which device is used to scan bar code items in supermarkets?
questions.explanation: Bar code readers are used to scan items in supermarkets and industrial products.

questions.stem: What type of memory is compared to a 'scratchpad' or 'whiteboard'?
questions.explanation: RAM behaves like a scratchpad memory or whiteboard for temporary storage.

questions.stem: Which generation introduced high-level programming languages?
questions.explanation: High-level programming languages were introduced during the third generation (1964-1971).

questions.stem: Which robot is associated with the Mars mission in the text?
questions.explanation: The Mars rover is listed as an example of a fifth-generation robot.

questions.stem: What does the abbreviation ENIAC stand for?
questions.explanation: ENIAC stands for Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer.

questions.stem: What was used for data transfer and storage in the First Generation of computers?
questions.explanation: Magnetic drums were used for data transfer and storage during the first generation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of third-generation computers?
questions.explanation: The IBM-168/360/370 series are listed as prominent computers in the third generation.

questions.stem: What technology is implemented to design microprocessors in the fourth generation?
questions.explanation: VLSI technology was implemented to design microprocessors in the fourth generation.

questions.stem: Which company sponsored the Aurora supercomputer project?
questions.explanation: The Aurora project is under the sponsorship of the United States Department of Energy.

questions.stem: What differentiates an input device from an output device?

options.B: Input devices transfer data to the computer, output devices receive data from it

questions.explanation: The text states that input devices transfer data to the computer, while output data (devices) receive data from it.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT an example of scanning input devices?
questions.explanation: Joysticks are listed as input devices but not under the scanning category, which includes OMR, OCR, and barcode readers.

questions.stem: What is the primary and commonly used data entry device?
questions.explanation: The keyboard is described as the primary and commonly used data entry device.

questions.stem: What type of printer generates output by spraying ink droplets onto paper?
questions.explanation: Inkjet printers generate output by spraying ink droplets onto the paper through a small nozzle.

questions.stem: What is the motherboard's shape described as?
questions.explanation: The motherboard is described as being rectangular in shape.

questions.stem: Which component prevents excessive heat radiation inside the system unit?
questions.explanation: Cooling fans and heat sinks prevent excessive heat and maintain operating conditions.

questions.stem: What is the typical model number for a CMOS battery?
questions.explanation: The document states that the CMOS battery is mostly CR2032.

questions.stem: What device is used to connect two electronic devices for data, power, or media transmission?
questions.explanation: Computer ports connect interface points or sockets between two electronic devices.

questions.stem: Which port technology is described as 'newer and much faster' than serial or parallel ports?
questions.explanation: The document mentions that USB technology is newer and much faster than serial or parallel ports.

questions.stem: What material is a microchip's slab made of?
questions.explanation: Microchips are mounted on a small flat piece of silicon slab.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an antivirus software mentioned in the text?
questions.explanation: Kaspersky is listed as an example of antivirus software for computer maintenance.

questions.stem: What does 'real-time computing' mean in the context of embedded systems?

options.A: Computing that happens on the weekends
options.C: Computing that only uses internet time

questions.explanation: Embedded systems often work within pre-defined time, known as real-time computing.

questions.stem: What is the function of a 'decoder' in a satellite television set-top box?

options.B: To read a signal from the dish and send input to the TV

questions.explanation: The document states a decoder reads signals from the dish to operate the TV.

questions.stem: Which of these allows users to send data across public networks as if they were directly connected to a private network?
questions.explanation: A Virtual Private Network (VPN) extends a private network across a public network for secure data transmission.

questions.stem: What law is rendered 'ineffective' by the increasing number of transistors in multi-core technology?
questions.explanation: Multi-core technology utilization renders Moore's law ineffective with the growing number of transistors.

questions.stem: Which company is NOT mentioned as a multi-core processor manufacturer?
questions.explanation: AMD, ARM, Broadcom, Intel, and VIA are listed as companies implementing multi-core utilization.

questions.stem: What is the characteristic of computer maintenance known as 'Software maintenance'?

options.A: Cleaning the dust out of the case
options.B: Updating programs and removing unnecessary files

questions.explanation: Software maintenance involves updating programs, removing unnecessary files, and managing resources.

questions.stem: In the context of networking, what does 'ISP' stand for?
questions.explanation: The document mentions 'Internet Service Provider (ISP)' in the section on network cards.

questions.stem: Which device is a gateway device in a computer network?
questions.explanation: Routers are listed as examples of gateway devices in a network.

questions.stem: What is 'throughput' in a computer network?

options.B: The time elapsing between a resource request and its availability

questions.explanation: Performance is a function of throughput, which is the time elapsed between the request for a resource and its availability.

questions.stem: Which component is MOST responsible for directing the execution of instructions within the CPU?
questions.explanation: The Control Unit directs and coordinates the execution of instructions, while the ALU performs calculations.

questions.stem: A user saves a file, but loses unsaved changes after a sudden power outage. Which component caused this data loss?
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile memory and loses its content when power is turned off.

questions.stem: Which of the following operations would NOT typically be handled directly by the ALU?
questions.explanation: The ALU handles arithmetic and logical operations, not storage tasks.

questions.stem: Which storage device would retain data even after the system is powered off?
questions.explanation: SSD is non-volatile storage, unlike RAM, cache, and registers.

questions.stem: Which scenario BEST demonstrates the concept of versatility in computers?

options.A: A computer performing calculations very fast
options.B: A computer running multiple different types of applications
options.C: A computer storing large amounts of data
options.D: A computer operating continuously without rest

questions.explanation: Versatility refers to the ability to perform different kinds of tasks.

questions.stem: Which component would MOST directly affect how many bits a CPU can process at once?
questions.explanation: Word size determines how many bits a CPU can process in a single operation.

questions.stem: A system is designed to respond instantly to sensor input within strict time limits. What type of computing is this?
questions.explanation: Real-time computing operates within strict timing constraints.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST explains why transistors replaced vacuum tubes?

options.A: They were larger and easier to repair
options.C: They were smaller, faster, and more efficient

questions.explanation: Transistors improved size, efficiency, and reliability compared to vacuum tubes.

questions.stem: Which of the following would MOST likely require a workstation instead of a standard PC?
questions.explanation: Workstations are designed for high-performance tasks like simulations and engineering work.

questions.stem: Which component acts as a temporary high-speed buffer between the CPU and main memory?
questions.explanation: Cache memory stores frequently used data for faster access by the CPU.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the role of an operating system?

options.B: It acts as an interface between hardware, software, and users

questions.explanation: The OS manages communication between hardware, software, and users.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an embedded system?
questions.explanation: Embedded systems perform dedicated functions within larger systems.

questions.stem: If a computer can handle multiple tasks simultaneously by splitting them across cores, what is this process called?
questions.explanation: Multithreading splits tasks into smaller parts to run concurrently on multiple cores.

questions.stem: Which of the following would MOST improve system performance when running many applications at once?
questions.explanation: More RAM allows more applications to run simultaneously without slowing down.

questions.stem: Which network component is responsible for directing data packets between different networks?
questions.explanation: Routers forward data packets between different networks.
